overview: Turn the 2026-02-10 Orbital PoC static security audit (docs/05-reviews-audits/security/*) into a small, PR-sized remediation plan. Focus on preventing Docker secret leakage, constraining spikes to dev-only, preventing CSRF-by-side-effects in demo-prod, removing Host-derived loopback SSRF, establishing baseline security headers + CSP rollout, hardening demo-prod compose defaults, mitigating PDF ingest DoS, and unifying CSV export hardening. Additional medium items include non-root container runtime and removing Host-header dependent absolute URL generation.
goals: Prevent accidental inclusion of local .env* secrets in Docker images.
Make spikes endpoints dev-only with defense-in-depth for risky operations.
Prevent CSRF-by-side-effects in demo-prod via same-origin enforcement for mutations.
Remove Host-derived loopback SSRF behavior in viewer server code.
Establish baseline security headers ownership and a staged CSP rollout plan.
Harden demo-prod compose defaults (no DB host exposure; required env vars enforced).
Add a wall-clock timeout for PDF ingest to reduce DoS risk.
Mitigate CSV formula injection consistently across all CSV exports.
Run runtime containers as non-root and avoid Host-header dependent absolute URL generation.
nonGoals: Implement full authn/authz/RBAC or multi-tenant isolation.
Perform runtime probing, fuzzing, or external network scanning.
Perfect CSP in one step (CSP should be staged, starting report-only).
Comprehensive dependency CVE remediation via live registry scanning (pnpm audit was blocked in the audit environment).
successMetrics: Docker builds do not include .env/.env.* files in image layers (except explicit templates).
In demo-prod/prod, /api/spikes/* is unreachable even if SPIKES_ENABLED=1 is mis-set.
Cross-site POSTs cannot trigger demo-prod side effects (export/run/load-pack).
Viewer does not derive internal fetch targets from Host header.
Baseline security headers are present on representative routes; CSP rollout is documented and staged.
demo-prod compose does not publish Postgres on the host by default and fails fast on missing required env vars.
PDF ingest has a hard timeout; CSV exports mitigate formula injection everywhere.
Runtime container runs as non-root; exported URLs are not Host-header poisoned.

demoProdThreatModel.justification: Safe-by-default reduces operator footguns and keeps demo-prod closer to prod constraints.

spikesAvailability.decision: Spikes are dev-only always; never available in demo-prod/prod (even behind a token).
spikesAvailability.justification: Spikes are explicitly unsafe surfaces; token gates are misconfig-prone and easy to forget to rotate.

securityHeadersOwnership.decision: App-owned baseline security headers via Next headers() (next.config.js); infra/WAF may add on top but is not required.
securityHeadersOwnership.justification: Portable and repo-verifiable; avoids drift across deployments.

stories.title: Stop Docker secret leakage (SEC-001)
stories.description: As an operator, I want Docker builds to exclude local .env* files so secrets cannot be baked into image layers by accident.
acceptanceCriteria: .dockerignore excludes **/.env and **/.env.* while allowing explicit templates like .env.example.
Building the apps/web Dockerfile from a worktree containing apps/web/.env.local does not include that file in image layers.
Optional: CI guard fails if non-template .env* files appear in the Docker build context.

stories.title: Make spikes dev-only + harden spikes CSV export (SEC-002, SEC-007)
stories.description: As a developer, I want spikes endpoints to be impossible to expose outside dev and for spikes CSV exports to apply the same hardening as production exports.
acceptanceCriteria: assertSpikesEnabled requires ORBITAL_MODE=dev and/or NODE_ENV=development in addition to SPIKES_ENABLED=1.
In demo-prod/prod, spikes endpoints return 404/403 regardless of SPIKES_ENABLED.
Spikes CSV export reuses the hardened CSV escaping helper so formula-leading values are prefixed safely.

stories.title: Prevent demo-prod CSRF-by-side-effects (SEC-004)
stories.description: As an operator, I want demo-prod mutations to be same-origin so cross-site requests cannot trigger exports, runs, or other side effects.
acceptanceCriteria: In demo-prod, non-GET/HEAD requests are rejected unless Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site/Referer indicates same-origin.
JSON mutation endpoints enforce Content-Type: application/json (or equivalently safe policy).
Same-origin UI requests continue to work in demo-prod.

stories.title: Remove Host-derived loopback SSRF (SEC-003)
stories.description: As an operator, I want server-side fetches to not be influenced by Host headers to prevent loopback SSRF/port scanning in demo-prod/dev contexts.
acceptanceCriteria: Viewer code does not derive internal fetch origin from request Host header/port.
If internal HTTP remains, origin is canonical + allowlisted and Authorization is not forwarded to untrusted origins.

stories.title: Baseline security headers + staged CSP rollout (SEC-005)
stories.description: As a developer, I want baseline security headers and a staged CSP plan so clickjacking and content-sniffing protections are explicit and consistent.
acceptanceCriteria: Baseline headers are set consistently (X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, clickjacking defense via frame-ancestors).
CSP rollout is staged (report-only first) and accounts for the inline script in apps/web/app/layout.tsx (nonce or refactor).

stories.title: Harden demo-prod compose defaults (SEC-008, SEC-010)
stories.description: As an operator, I want demo-prod compose to avoid DB host exposure and fail fast when critical secrets are missing.
acceptanceCriteria: docker-compose.demo-prod.yml does not publish Postgres to the host by default (no 5432:5432).
Required env vars use ${VAR:?required} syntax for signing secret and basic auth creds.
Optional: docker-compose.yml is documented or adjusted to reduce copy/paste footguns.

stories.title: Add PDF ingest wall-clock timeout (SEC-006)
stories.description: As an operator, I want PDF ingest to fail closed with a timeout to reduce DoS risk from worst-case PDFs.
acceptanceCriteria: PDF ingest has a per-document wall-clock timeout.
Timeout failure returns a safe user-facing error and does not leak internals.

stories.title: Run runtime containers as non-root (Report-RP #9)
stories.description: As an operator, I want the runtime container to run as non-root to reduce blast radius if an RCE is introduced.
acceptanceCriteria: apps/web Dockerfile runtime stage runs as a non-root user.
demo-prod compose still works with mounted volumes (object store remains writable).

stories.title: Avoid Host-header dependent absolute URL generation (Report-RP #10)
stories.description: As a developer, I want exported URLs to be relative or derived from trusted config so Host header poisoning cannot influence absolute URLs.
acceptanceCriteria: Endpoints do not use new URL(req.url).origin to generate absolute URLs unless origin is trusted/allowlisted.
Relative URLs are preferred where possible, or PUBLIC_ORIGIN is used with an allowlist.

automated: Add focused tests for spikes gating and CSV escaping reuse.
Add focused tests for middleware same-origin enforcement (where feasible).
manualSmoke: docker build -f apps/web/Dockerfile . (confirm no .env* files are included in layers without printing secrets).
In demo-prod, attempt a cross-site POST to a state-changing endpoint and confirm it is rejected.
In demo-prod, request /api/spikes/* and confirm it is blocked even if SPIKES_ENABLED=1.
In viewer, attempt to influence Host header and confirm internal fetch destinations do not change.
Check response headers on representative routes (baseline headers present).
docker compose -f docker-compose.demo-prod.yml up (missing required env vars should fail fast; Postgres not published on host).
